messages.author: 5b4763d3a422c983
messages.subject: Intergration failing in parboot
parts:
I am having issues evaluating goodness of fit for distsamp models. Bootstrapping is returning the error, "the integral is probably divergent". Any ideas on why integration would be failing? Is there any way to fix the issue? I'm using version 0.11-0 of unmarked.


###
m32.hazfit <- distsamp(~conifer ~conifer +ce, umf, keyfun="hazard", output="density", unitsOut="kmsq", control=list(maxit=1000))

(fm <- m32.hazfit)

#
fitstats <- function(fm) {
  observed <- getY(fm@data)
  expected <- fitted(fm)
  resids <- residuals(fm)
  sse <- sum(resids^2)
  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
  return(out)
}

(pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=10, report=1))

t0 = 33.91334 442.937 37.39686
Error in integrate(gxhaz, db[j], db[j + 1], shape = shape[i], scale = scale,  :
  the integral is probably divergent

messages.author: 5b4763d3a422c983
messages.subject: Re: Intergration failing in parboot
parts: I thought it might be helpful to post some additional details in the hopes that someone might be able to help. I am completely new to unmarked, working on a project I've just taken over from a postdoc who left for a permanent position. The data are from line transect aerial surveys of moose, and we're looking to do just the basics with it for now (i.e., estimate densities). We have several covariates we think might influence detection and/or density, so I went through model selection with models of every possible combination of our covariates and selected the top model for further analysis. Logically the covariates influencing both detection and density in top model make sense, but I am unable to evaluate goodness of fit with parboot as integration is failing. I am not sure if this is an issue with my code, the model, the data, etc. I found one older, somewhat similar question in the group about this error message, and the suggestion was to specify a lower relative tolerance for integration (i.e. rel.tol = 0.001). I tried this with the model but integration still fails.

###

    output = "density", unitsOut = "kmsq", control = list(maxit = 1000))

ce              2.34 0.925  2.53 1.14e-02

shape(Intercept)      4.5  2.34  1.93  0.0537
shapeconifer        -31.7 13.32 -2.38  0.0173

Hazard-rate(scale):
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
    0.248 0.491 0.506   0.613

AIC: 195.9955
 
> fitstats <- function(fm) {
+   observed <- getY(fm@data)
+   expected <- fitted(fm)
+   resids <- residuals(fm)
+   sse <- sum(resids^2, na.rm = TRUE)
+   chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected, na.rm = TRUE)
+   freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
+   out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
+   return(out)
+ }
> (pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=10, report=1))

Error in integrate(gxhaz, db[j], db[j + 1], shape = shape[i], scale = scale,  :
  the integral is probably divergent
>

I would greatly appreciate if anyone could help lend some clarity to this issue.

Thank you.

It might be worth trying a different scale for distance. Are you using meters or kilometers? Convert to the one you aren't using and change the "unitsIn" argument.

Richard
